correctness.rationale: With 0<t,a,b<1 and identical Markov law for 3- and 4-cell observations, only 000, 101 and 0000 respectively realize (R3=0), (R3=2) and (R4=0). A=t(1-a)^2, B=(1-t)ba, C=t(1-a)^3 imply the unique inverse t=A^3/C^2, a=1-C/A, b=BAC^2/((C^2-A^3)(A-C)). Their open-unit-interval constraints are exactly 0<C<A, A^3<C^2, and 0<B<((C^2-A^3)(A-C))/(AC^2), giving both necessity and sufficiency. Flux balance yields stationarity iff BC^2=A(A-C)^2. Positive square roots of A and B identify t,a,b uniquely within the stationary family, with precise feasible inequality (sqrt(A)+sqrt(B))(sqrt(A)+2sqrt(B))<1. Two explicit different stationary triples share the 2-site patch law. The transfer matrix predicts all n. An exact Fraction checker compared 10,800 entire distributions across 1,350 finite parameter triples and 688,500 enumerated words; this is supporting finite evidence, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Short-window Markov-run distributions and matrix/renewal generating functions are acknowledged forward-method prior art. The claimed combined exact inverse of three ecological patch-count probabilities, an if-and-only-if semialgebraic feasible image, a parameter-free stationarity identity, and the sharp stationarity-specific single-window threshold were compared by mathematical implication, not title only. No inspected source or returned mathematical record explicitly supplied this complete inverse statement. The closely related 2004 joint run-count paper was accessible only through its abstract, so equivalence or a derivable corollary remains a meaningful unresolved bibliographic risk; the present review does not claim priority has been independently certified.

value.rationale: Landscape transects frequently preserve histogram counts of fragmented occupied patches while individual cell patterns are unavailable or compressed. The theorem completely characterizes which three scalar, natural patch-count statistics uniquely identify the two spatial correlation transitions plus starting occupancy, states every feasibility constraint (so observed population statistics can be diagnosed), distinguishes stationary from general initial laws, and proves the exact minimum window length to identify a stationary model. This is a natural, sharp complete inverse classification not an arbitrary parameter slice or mere verification of a known table. No claim of finite-sample robustness, higher-dimensional habitat dynamics, or original forward PGF theory is made.
